newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia seeks extradition of suspected paedophile.
newsitem.headline: Australia seeks extradition of suspected paedophile.

text.p: Australian Attorney-General Daryl Williams on Tuesday said he had signed a formal extradition request for a suspected Australian paedophile being held in custody South Africa.
Philip Bell, arrested by police two weeks ago at the South African surfing town of Jeffreys Bay, has been charged in Australia with 215 sex offences relating to boys aged 10 to 18.
"I have instructed my department to ensure that the relevant documentation reaches the South African authorities without delay," Williams said in a statement.
"I am advised that delivery through diplomatic channels should be accomplished by the end of this week," he said.
Bell, who says he wants to return to Australia to clear his name, is due to appear in court on February 4 for his extradition hearing.
Australia has already sent a police officer from its child protection task force to South Africa to make a formal plea for extradition of the wealthy 62-year-old businessman.
